g.text: Six Seconds Inside the Click
What happens between the ad click and the recorded conversion, step by step
T+0ms — user clicks the ad
Platform records the click against the campaign, ad set,
ad and creative in real time.
T+50ms — click ID appended to URL
Auto-tagging adds gclid (Google) / fbclid (Meta) / ttclid (TikTok).
Redirect passes through the platform's tracker domain.
URL now looks like: yoursite.com/?gclid=Cj0KCQ...
T+1s — landing page loads
Browser fetches your site. Base tag (gtag / Pixel) loads
in the head and starts listening.
T+2s — click ID stored in first-party cookie
Cookie written to the site's own domain: _gcl_aw (Google) /
_fbp (Meta) / _ttp (TikTok). Lasts 30-90 days depending
on the platform's attribution window.
T+minutes/days — user browses, then converts
Purchases, fills a form, signs up. The event tag fires
on the converting page or from the form submit.
T+conversion — event sent with stored click ID
Pixel / gtag sends the conversion event including the
stored click ID and a unique event_id. Server-side CAPI
sends a parallel event with hashed identity.
T+seconds — platform matches and records
Event_id dedup happens, attribution window is checked,
conversion credited to campaign ▸ ad set ▸ ad.
Algorithm now has a new training example.
RESULT: Ads Manager shows the conversion against the
original click. Smart Bidding now knows this user converted.
Sources: Google Ads auto-tagging (support.google.com/google-ads/answer/3095550),
Conversion Linker cookies (support.google.com/tagmanager/answer/7549390). Retrieved 24 Sep 2026.
